newsitem.title: UK: UK denies minister has conflict of interest.
newsitem.headline: UK denies minister has conflict of interest.

text.p: The British government on Wednesday denied Lord David Simon, minister for trade and competitiveness in Europe and former chairman of British Petroleum Plc, had a conflict of interest over a European Union action plan.

John Redwood, trade and industry spokesman of the main Conservative opposition party, said earlier that Simon had approved the plan covering four areas that directly affect BP, including liberalisation of the EU gas market.
He said this put Simon in breach of procedures for ministers designed to avoid conflicts of interest and called on him to resign.

The Department of Trade and Industry said Simon had signed an explanatory memorandum summarising for parliament the European Commission's action plan for the single market, which had been approved by EU heads of state in Amsterdam in June.
"Lord Simon is the minister for trade and competitiveness in Europe and the single market is one of his prime responsibilities.

"There is no conflict of interest in his signing this document. Issues such as tax, state aids policy and biotechnology, which we understand are causing concern to Mr Redwood, are not areas relating specifically to BP," the ministry said.
A spokesman said the document contained just one passing reference to gas liberalisation as an area where the single market was still incomplete.
He said Simon was not precluded from seeing papers on such issues but would not participate in any decisions with a direct bearing on BP.
